name: Gulganj–Chaibasa Highway
aka: Formed from parts of the former NH 78, NH 23 and NH 33
history: NH 43 winds across the mineral-rich heart of eastern-central India. It begins at Gulganj in the Bundelkhand region of Madhya Pradesh, passes the marble and limestone town of Katni, crosses the coal belts around Shahdol and Ambikapur, and climbs the forested plateaus of Chhattisgarh and Jharkhand to reach Ranchi. It ends at Chaibasa, the centre of a big iron-ore mining district. The route was stitched together in the 2010 renumbering from parts of the old NH 78, NH 23 and NH 33.
facts: Runs for more than 1,000 km across Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh and Jharkhand.
Passes through Umaria district, the gateway to Bandhavgarh National Park.
Serves some of India's biggest coal and iron-ore mining areas.
Ranchi, the capital of Jharkhand, is the largest city on the route.
